::: {.entry-meta}
[decision]{.chip .decision} Entry 13 · milestone M1
:::

M1 ends in a review by a physicist, the milestone's human gate. Every M1 task was built and
the other three acceptance criteria were met (entries 8, 11 and 12). Open for the review were
the tolerance for the published benchmark, which the brief leaves to the physicist ([OQ-5](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-5)), and
the choice of fallback transport model ([OQ-1](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-1)). The owner did the review as reviewer of record.
The agent set out six items, each with its evidence and a recommendation. The owner accepted
all six as written. The full list is on the [decisions page](../decisions.qmd#m1-review).

## What was decided

| item | decision |
|---|---|
| benchmark tolerance | against RAPTOR, [profiles ≤ 2% (densities ≤ 0.1%), traces ≤ 5%]{.claim}[C-061](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-061){.cid .st-reviewed}; fusion and Ohmic powers reported, not gated. Result: [T_i 1.23% (1.1%), T_e 0.28% (0.71%), n_e 0.03% (0.03%), psi 0.49% (0.41%), q 0.69% (0.70%)]{.claim}[C-050](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-050){.cid .st-reviewed}, transient [2.4% at dt = 0.05 s, 2.9% at dt = 0.00625 s (1.0% at t = 10 s)]{.claim}[C-053](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-053){.cid .st-reviewed}; both pass |
| TORAX version | the change from the paper's TORAX run ([T_i 0.13%, T_e 0.50%, n_e 0.01%, psi 0.08%, q 0.16%; Ohmic power density 3.6%]{.claim}[C-051](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-051){.cid .st-reviewed}) accepted as a code-version effect |
| pedestal | the pinning source removes [87–98%]{.claim}[C-038](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-038){.cid .st-reviewed} of the heating; accepted for core profiles, edge power not taken from these runs ([K-010](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-010)) |
| time step | the ITER hybrid example settings check the wrapper only; physics reference runs use a step converged in time to the limit on the [decisions page](../decisions.qmd#m1-review) |
| ASCOT5 | orbit tolerance 10^-7^; 640 alphas give totals ([72.2 MW vs 70.5 MW]{.claim}[C-059](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-059){.cid .st-reviewed}) and the electron/ion split; the radial shape waits for the queued production run; an unexplained excess in birth power ([K-011](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-011)) to be found before beam ions |
| fallback | TORAX's Bohm/gyro-Bohm model; the critical-gradient model stays in the analytic test loop |

## What changed in the code

The tolerance is now part of the benchmark: the limits sit in the benchmark module, a
regression test fails if any gated quantity leaves them, and the benchmark command prints each
quantity against its limit. Two known limits were added to the ceilings list: the pedestal
pinning ([K-010](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-010)) and the alpha birth-power excess ([K-011](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-011)). The claims that the review judged are
now marked *reviewed* in the [claims register](../claims.qmd).

**Where this stands**: M1 has passed its acceptance criteria and its human gate. The ASCOT5
production run ([OQ-13](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-13)) continues as follow-up work and does not reopen the gate. M2 (training
data) starts once the owner provides access to the turbulence code and its licence terms, the
operating space to sample, and a compute allocation.
